title: The City That Never Forgets
lines: Floating City was not built on land. It was built on debt. Every brick, every neon sign, every gilded elevator was purchased with a promise — and in Floating City, promises were the only currency more valuable than blood.

Qian Ye arrived with nothing: no money, no identity chip, no past that the city's databases could verify. This was intentional. He had erased his own history to escape something — or someone. The city did not care. It welcomed everyone.

Within a week, Qian Ye had accumulated a debt of three million credits to the Red Lotus Bank. This was also intentional. In Floating City, the deeper your debt, the more the system protected you. A man who owed nothing was disposable. A man who owed millions was an asset.

His plan was simple: use the initial debt to infiltrate the inner circles of the city's power structure, then execute the single, catastrophic hack that would erase not just his own debt, but the entire credit system.
